difficulty_reason: For a locally Noetherian scheme X with dualizing complex omega_X and dimension function delta, and a coherent module F, the lemma with E^i = SheafExt^{-i}(F, omega_X) asserts that each E^i is coherent and that for x in X: E^i_x is nonzero only for delta(x) <= i <= delta(x) + dim(Supp(F_x)); the dimension of the support of E^{i+delta(x)}_x is at most i; depth(F_x) is the smallest i >= 0 with E^{i+delta(x)}_x nonzero; and x lies in the support of the sum of E^j for j <= i exactly when depth(F_x) + delta(x) <= i (statement lines 587-629). Coherence is Lemma labelled lemma-dualizing-schemes (proof lines 631-634). Choosing an affine neighbourhood of x, Derived Categories of Schemes, Lemma labelled perfect-lemma-quasi-coherence-internal-hom and More on Algebra, Lemma labelled more-algebra-lemma-base-change-RHom part (3) identify the stalk E^i_x with Ext^{-i}_{O_{X,x}}(F_x, omega_{X,x}) = Ext^{delta(x)-i}(F_x, omega_{X,x}[-delta(x)]), and by the construction of delta in Lemma labelled lemma-dimension-function-scheme this reduces parts (1), (2) and (3) to Dualizing Complexes, Lemma labelled dualizing-lemma-sitting-in-degrees, while part (4) is a formal consequence of (3) and (1) (proof lines 634-646). Shifting by the dimension function to normalise the complex and then reading the statements off the algebraic dualizing complex is the non-formal step, so the claim is H2.
